content: 1. The World Health Organization published a report in January 2007 titled Multi-country Regional Pooled Procurement of Medicines, which spans pages 1 to 39. 2. Khetrapal Singh P and Travis P discussed strategies to accelerate access to essential medicines in the WHO South-East Asia Region, emphasizing opportunities for enhanced engagement and improved evidence. This was published in the WHO South-East Asia Journal of Public Health in 2018, volume 7, issue 2, pages 59–61. 3. Espín J and colleagues explored how voluntary cross-border collaboration in public procurement can enhance access to health technologies in Europe. This was detailed in a 2016 policy brief, issue 21. 4. Ferraresi M, Gucciardi G, and Rizzo L examined whether centralized purchasing reduces public expenditure, presenting evidence from the Italian healthcare system. Their findings were published in the journal Società Italiana di Economia Pubblica in 2017, issue 732. 5. Toulemon L analyzed the impact of group purchasing on the prices hospitals pay for medicines. This study was published in the journal Health Economics (United Kingdom) in 2018, volume 27, issue 9, pages 1380–1393. 6. Baldi S and Vannoni D investigated the effects of centralization on pharmaceutical procurement prices, focusing on the role of institutional quality and corruption. Their research appeared in the journal Regional Studies in 2017, volume 51, issue 3, pages 426–438. 7. Dubois P, Lefouili Y, and Straub S studied the pooled procurement of drugs in lowand middle-income countries. Their findings were accessible as of August 21, 2020, in a PDF document. 8. Kim SW and Skordis-Worrall J conducted a case study on whether voluntary pooled procurement can reduce the price of antiretroviral drugs, specifically Efavirenz. Their research was published in Health Policy and Planning in 2017, volume 32, issue 4, pages 516–526. 9. Barbosa K de S and Fiuza E analyzed the effects of demand aggregation and credit risk in pooled procurement, using evidence from Brazilian public purchases of pharmaceuticals and medical supplies. This was documented in the C-Micro Working Paper Series, Report No. 299, published by the Escola de Economia de São Paulo, Fundação Getulio Vargas, São Paulo, in 2011. 10. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) provided information on the PAHO Strategic Fund, which can be accessed online. 11. Mamiya H provided an update on the drug pricing system in Japan, with the document accessible as of August 29, 2020, in PDF format. 12. The Office of Fair Trade released a report in November 2007 titled The Pharmaceutical Price Regulation Scheme, available in PDF format. 13. A document titled Trade in Pharmaceutical Products was accessible as of August 21, 2020, in PDF format. 14. Bauer M examined the compounding effects of tariffs on medicines, estimating the real cost of protectionism in emerging markets. This study was published in the European Centre for International Political Economy and was accessible as of August 29, 2020, in PDF format. 15. Creese A authored Working Paper 5: Sales Taxes on Medicines, which was accessible as of August 29, 2020, in PDF format.
